data.title: MISSION SUCCESS: Rocket Lab Launches 101st Electron Mission
data.description:
MAHIA, New Zealand, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rocket Lab Corporation (Nasdaq: RKLB), a global leader in launch services and space systems, today successfully completed another dedicated Electron launch for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite operator Synspective.

The ‘Night Owls Never Sleep’ mission launched from Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1 in New Zealand at 1:15 p.m. NZDT on 27 September 2026, delivering the 14h StriX satellite directly into a 569km low Earth orbit. This latest addition further scales Synspective’s Earth-observation constellation that gathers high-resolution images of the planet's surface regardless of weather conditions or time of day.

Today’s mission was Rocket Lab’s 22nd launch of 2026 and 101st mission overall, extending Electron’s lead as the world’s most frequently-launched small-lift orbital rocket.

Mission Highlights:

  • Unmatched Track Record: Maintaining a 100% mission success rate for Synspective, Rocket Lab has been the sole launch provider for all 14 StriX satellites to date.
  • Rapid Constellation Building: As Rocket Lab’s 22nd mission of the year, today’s launch highlights Electron’s high-cadence reliability that commercial constellation operators depend on to scale their operations on schedule.
  • Record-Breaking Partnership: Following a historic 20-launch deal signed in September - the largest commercial contract for Electron to date - Synspective is Rocket Lab’s largest launch customer with 47 total missions booked. Today’s launch leaves 33 dedicated missions on the manifest to be launched through 2031, giving Synspective long-term certainty as they build out their constellation.

‘Night Owls Never Sleep’ launch images: click here

‘Night Owls Never Sleep’ launch broadcast: click here

Rocket Lab Media Contact
Murielle Baker
media@rocketlabusa.com

About Rocket Lab
Rocket Lab (Nasdaq: RKLB) is an end-to-end space company delivering rockets, satellites, and spacecraft components for commercial, government, and defense missions. Driven by its industry-leading small-lift rockets Electron and HASTE and its upcoming reusable Neutron medium-lift rocket, Rocket Lab delivers reliable and responsive launch for the world’s most important missions from constellation deployment to missile defense. Rocket Lab’s satellites and components have powered more than 1,700 missions in Earth orbit, as well as deep-space exploration of the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Learn more at www.rocketlabcorp.com.

data.title: I hate that Jensen Huang is back at Nvidia, but I love what it's done for my 401(k). Am I a hypocrite?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

Doing nothing and maintaining an even temperament is often the work of gods

Jensen Huang, who on Monday returned as CEO of Nvidia. (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

I was paralyzed during the market downturn, so I have a question in the event that this bounce - led by the shocking and, in my opinion, unwelcome news that Jensen Huang has returned as Nvidia's (NVDA) CEO - does not last. No comment on that, as it happens, even though I have my opinions, like most people do.

I'm writing to you about my own strategy, not to pass judgment on other people's corporate decisions. During a market downturn, is it better for me to draw down cash from CDs for the next year or two rather than taking money from my equities and annuities at a loss? Where are the safe havens? I don't want to eat into my retirement savings.

Planning Ahead

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: America is divided into two countries - Trump's pro-billionaires and Mamdani's anti-billionaires

Being paralyzed during the recent volatility in the market is not exactly a bad thing.

Dear Planning,

It's fair to say that many people were surprised by Jensen Huang's return on Monday - and you are not alone in having strong opinions on that.

Some of the same people who cried foul over the fall in their 401(k)s and IRAs may well be rolling their eyes over the return of Huang to the helm of Nvidia, which now appears to be the cornerstone of the AI revolution, mostly due to its multibillion-dollar microchip business and proprietary software ecosystem. Indeed, the stock gave up some of Monday's gains on Tuesday as investors turned their attention to regulatory concerns about the export of U.S. microchips to China and elsewhere. Huang was effectively fired (he officially resigned) from the company a couple of weeks ago over his reported affairs with two employees, as well as one with a woman who has been accused of being a Chinese spy.

Commentators have questioned whether President Donald Trump overlooked the potential and alleged national-security threat by calling for Huang's return to Nvidia NVDA, thereby signaling that the company is too big to fail. Others bemoaned the decision by the company's board and wondered what the role of such boards is, if not to uphold professional, legal and personal standards. While low-wage American workers have been fired over bathroom breaks, skeptics may wonder if rules of conduct only apply to nonbillionaires.

It's OK to have joys and concerns about the billionaire class and your 401(k), even if the answers conflict with each other.

And, honestly, being paralyzed during the recent volatility in the market is not exactly a bad thing, either. Doing nothing and maintaining an even temperament is often the work of gods. Some people panic and sell, or move into real estate, bonds, or gold, and constantly check their 401(k) while getting upset over paper losses. Yet short-term swings won't have a big impact if they aren't about to retire or haven't just retired - especially if they have cash alternatives. How many times a day or week did you check your 401(k) when the market was on the rise? I'm guessing not a lot.

I sympathize with your urge to check. According to a 2026 report by the Investment Company Institute (ICI), a global trade association representing regulated funds and their shareholders, 81% of mutual fund-owning U.S. households hold stock funds - most of them inside workplace retirement plans. Because broad stock and index funds are heavily weighted toward mega-cap AI leaders like Nvidia, a significant share of American households are naturally exposed to those stocks. "Mutual funds play a key role in their households' balance sheets," the researchers wrote.

But back to the other questions in your letter: Yes, drawing from CDs and relying on annuity income can be a smart move. That assumes you don't have required minimum distributions from a traditional retirement account and your CDs have reached the end of their term. If you paid extra for a guaranteed lifetime income rider on your annuities - locking in an income stream if markets plummet or your account balance falls to zero - that will protect you during a correction, while fixed annuities aren't tied to the market's fortunes at all. Having cash alternatives helps you avoid "sequence-of-returns risk," where poor market performance in the early years of retirement puts pressure on a portfolio you're drawing from.

Don't miss: 'Nvidia's turmoil has me spooked': Is it time to sell my stocks and buy real estate?

Timing the market vs. managing risk

Darius Dale, founder and CEO of 42 Macro, a macroeconomic research and systematic risk-management firm, predicts that markets will return to a "risk-on market regime," where investors favor higher risk assets over safe havens, within a couple of months. "Hope is not an effective risk-management process," he says. "Positioning for the market regime helps investors avoid fear of missing out (FOMO) and fear of more losses (FOML). FOMO causes investors to buy cycle tops, and FOML causes investors to sell cycle lows. These are the two worst things any investor can do to their financial well-being."

As for your curiosity about safe havens, I can understand why you would consider them after such a volatile week, especially with lingering questions about the stock market's heavy dependence on AI. The right mix depends on your risk tolerance and, as Dale suggested, your expectations about the economic outlook, especially if you want to factor in how reliant the economy is becoming on AI. There are many paths to take. Andrew Clinton, CEO of Clinton Investment Management, suggests municipal bonds as a haven during a correction.

I can understand why you would look for safe havens, especially with lingering questions about the market's heavy dependence on AI.

Municipal bonds are, for the record, more appropriate for investors in higher tax brackets with money held in taxable accounts who live in high-tax states, and for retirees prioritizing cash flow and capital preservation. "Municipal bonds offer attractive tax-adjusted carry and stable underlying asset-class credit quality for investors seeking durable cash flows amidst equity-market volatility," he says. "Current municipal bond yields remain near the most attractive levels in decades."

Clinton also has a rosier outlook on the underlying strength of the U.S. economy than, perhaps, many folks. "Credit fundamentals remain strong, with default rates representing only a fraction of corporate default rates," he says. "Municipal issuers provide essential services such as airports, utilities and toll roads, generating durable cash flows with limited exposure to corporate earnings volatility. If inflation moderates and rates decline, municipals offer the potential for both attractive income and capital appreciation."

For other safe havens, consider shorter-duration bonds, mutual funds and exchange-traded funds that invest in bonds with maturities of less than five years, as well as Treasury inflation-protected securities (TIPS) backed by the U.S. Treasury to guard against rising prices. Give a thought to value-oriented and defensive sectors, including consumer-staples, utilities and healthcare stocks, for retired investors who seek stability over higher returns. Your lifestyle, the balances in your retirement accounts, your goals, your financial profile - whether you have a mortgage, debt or long-term-care insurance - and your views on AI all play a role.

Pausing during a storm does not mean you suffer from paralysis, and you don't have to like the news in order to plan around it.

Your letter attests to that.

Related: Is Social Security a Ponzi scheme? No. Don't get carried away with 1930s-era prophecies of doom.

data.title: CCTV4: Bringing Classical Chinese Poetry to the World Documentary Premiere One Poem, One World
data.description:
CCTV4: Bringing Classical Chinese Poetry to the World Documentary Premiere One Poem, One World

CCTV4: Bringing Classical Chinese Poetry to the World Documentary Premiere One Poem, One World

PR Newswire

BEIJING, Nov. 26, 2026

BEIJING, Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Classical Chinese poetry has a history dating back thousands of years. It enjoyed a golden age during the Tang and Song dynasties, from the 8th to the 13th centuries, when poets such as Li Bai, Du Fu, Su Shi and Li Qingzhao flourished. Their works, while often depicting common human emotions and simple details of everyday life, are celebrated for their power also to embody the wisdom and spirit of the Chinese nation.

Yet, despite its ancient origins, classical Chinese poetry retains surprising resonance still today, as a brand new CMG television production reveals. Starting from the real-life experiences of several foreign nationals living in China, One Poem, One World employs accessible interpretations and authentic, moving stories to closely link classical poetry with contemporary life. By referring to Three Hundred Tang Poems, an anthology compiled in the mid-18th century, and Poems by a Thousand Masters, containing verses from both the Tang and the Song dynasties, One Poem, One World invites audiences in China and abroad to discover, through the medium of classical poetry, more about Chinese culture, and the lifestyle, values and spiritual pursuits of Chinese people.

Launched in conjunction with the 2026 World Chinese Language Conference, One Poem, One World aims, in six episodes, to promote Chinese language learning, the study of traditional Chinese culture and literary exchanges with other countries.

The first episode of One Poem, One World airs on CCTV-4, the Chinese International Channel of China Media Group, on November 29.

data.title: Australia Orders LNG Exporters Reserve Some Gas to Plug Shortages at Home
data.description:
By Rhiannon Hoyle

Australia will require liquefied natural gas exporters to reserve up to a fifth of their shipments for the domestic market to help lower power bills for local households and businesses.

The law, approved early Friday, comes amid forecasts of supply shortfalls along the country's densely populated east coast--including Sydney and Melbourne--as traditional local gas fields deplete. The requirement takes effect Jan. 1, 2028, to align with industry contracting cycles, officials said.

"Australia has abundant gas resources and Australians should benefit from them," said Resources Minister Madeleine King. "This scheme will make more Australian gas available to our households and businesses, putting downward pressure on prices."

Australia is among the world's largest LNG exporters following significant investment by companies such as ConocoPhillips and Shell. The majority of Australian LNG is shipped to Japan, China, and South Korea, with about three-quarters sold under long-term contracts.

data.title: TCL CSOT Showcases Value Chain Collaboration at DTC2026, From Materials to End-Device Applications
data.description:
TCL CSOT Showcases Value Chain Collaboration at DTC2026, From Materials to End-Device Applications

TCL CSOT Showcases Value Chain Collaboration at DTC2026, From Materials to End-Device Applications

PR Newswire

WUHAN, China, Nov. 26, 2026

WUHAN, China, Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TCL CSOT's 2026 Global Display Tech-Ecosystem Conference (DTC2026), held under the theme "True Vision, AI in Motion," brought together partners from across the global display industry to showcase advances in materials, joint technology development, and end-device applications. The event highlighted how collaboration among upstream suppliers, panel manufacturers, and end-device partners can turn individual technological breakthroughs into integrated solutions and broader commercial applications, with IJP OLED at the center of TCL CSOT's practice.

Upstream Collaboration: Advancing Display Materials

At DTC2026, TCL CSOT and its upstream partners, including AGC, 3M, Merck, Summer Sprout, NOVATEK, Mitsubishi, SFC, SKMJ, and Idemitsu (IK), presented developments spanning advanced packaging, optical materials, display-driving technologies, and key materials for IJP OLED.

In advanced packaging, AGC showcased its TGV Glass Substrates for Advanced Packaging, featuring fine-pitch through-glass vias (TGVs) and high-precision through-glass via fabrication. The technology supports mass production of 510 × 515 mm large-format glass substrates for advanced packaging.

In optical materials, 3M presented several solutions for foldable displays, augmented reality (AR), and automotive applications. These included its Low Modulus Foldable OCA CEF94, Film-based Waveguide AR Glasses Demo, Optical Solution for Auto Under Display Camera, and Light Control Film for Auto OLED Display. CEF94 passed bending tests at temperatures as low as -30°C, helping reduce foldable-display creases under low-temperature conditions.

For emerging optical systems, Merck demonstrated its PB-Lens concept, which uses reactive mesogen (RM) materials and thin-film processing to explore the potential of planar lenses in virtual reality (VR) optical systems. Meanwhile, NOVATEK showcased its NOVA 14" WU + TED display and NOVA Privacy Display, highlighting advances in display-driving architecture and visual privacy that support lower-power designs and a wider range of end-device applications.

As IJP OLED advances toward broader commercialization, partners also presented key emissive materials and printing inks. Summer Sprout'sY4 red IJP-ink achieves 100% DCI-P3 color gamut coverage and improves device lifetime by more than 40% compared with the Y3 material system. Mitsubishi's IJP FLB INK uses solution-processable B Prime materials, increasing device brightness and efficiency (BI) by 10% while maintaining stable lifetime performance. SFC's IJP EML-B INK features BH-BD materials with approximately 50% improved solubility, supporting precision inkjet printing for high-PPI displays. SKMJ's IJP Blue Dopant delivers approximately 30% longer device lifetime than the Y3 system, while Idemitsu's IJP Blue Host improves Y4 device efficiency by 4% over Y3 through optimized molecular structures and host-guest matching.

Together, these developments across red, blue, and host materials strengthen the material foundation for IJP OLED. By bringing upstream materials expertise together with TCL CSOT's panel R&D and manufacturing capabilities, these collaborations help align materials development with actual product requirements and support the broader commercialization of IJP OLED technology.

Bringing Display Technologies into End-Device Applications

At DTC2026, TCL CSOT joined Lenovo, MSI, TAL Education Group, and VOYAH to showcase applications across laptops, desktop monitors, gaming handhelds, smart education, and automotive displays.

With Lenovo, TCL CSOT presented products across PC and professional display segments. The Lenovo Legion R9000P 16.0 WQ IJP OLED Display combines a 2560 × 1600 resolution with a 240Hz refresh rate. Its Real Stripe RGB pixel arrangement reduces color fringing around text, supporting both clear text and smooth gaming visuals. The Lenovo Legion Y900 11 features an 11.1-inch 3.8K LTPS display with a 144Hz refresh rate, delivering high-resolution visuals and smooth performance to mobile entertainment and content creation. Meanwhile, the ThinkVision P27UL-40, a 27-inch 4K IJP OLED professional monitor, combines a 120Hz refresh rate with high color gamut coverage to support business productivity and professional creative work.

TCL CSOT and MSI jointly presented devices for gaming and business use. The MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ features an 8-inch 120Hz IPS display with Variable Refresh Rate (VRR), helping deliver smoother gaming visuals. The MSI Prestige 14 AI+ uses a 14-inch IJP OLED display, combining wide color gamut coverage with a fast response time for mobile productivity and creative applications. For desktop users, the MSI PRO MAX OLED 271UPJW12 IJP OLED Display features TCL CSOT's proprietary Real Stripe RGB pixel arrangement to improve text clarity and reduce color fringing. It also incorporates MSI OLED Auto Care technology, which uses Dynamic Data Cumulative Compensation (DCC) to perform background OLED maintenance automatically, without interrupting normal use. The MSI MAG 346CQDF E20 Dual-Mode Curved Gaming Monitor offers two display modes: 200Hz at full resolution and up to 400Hz in HD mode, catering to different gaming requirements.

Spanning an 8-inch gaming handheld, an 11.1-inch tablet, 14-inch laptops, and 27-inch desktop monitors, these products illustrate how TCL CSOT and its end-device partners are adapting display technologies to different sizes, form factors, and user experiences.

Building a More Connected Display Ecosystem

At DTC2026, TCL CSOT highlighted efforts to extend partnerships beyond individual projects to technical standards, shared R&D platforms, and longer-term industry collaboration. Discussions included the new TÜV Rheinland Native Gaming Performance Display Standard, the Wuhan Joint Laboratory, and related ecosystem partnerships. TCL CSOT's IJP OLED roadmap across its t12 and t8 facilities also creates opportunities to coordinate materials, manufacturing processes, and end-device requirements across the supply chain, supporting the development and large-scale application of emerging display technologies.

From materials innovation by AGC, 3M, and Merck to end-device applications with Lenovo, MSI, and TAL Education Group, DTC2026 demonstrated how expertise across the value chain can turn technological advances into practical applications. Looking ahead, TCL CSOT will continue to work with global partners across materials research, panel manufacturing, and end-device applications, bringing together expertise from across the value chain to advance display technologies and expand and develop a more open, connected ecosystem.

About TCL CSOT

Established in 2009, TCL China Star Optoelectronics Technology Co., Ltd. (TCL CSOT) is a leading global innovator in display technologies. Its LCD, OLED, and MLED solutions power applications across TVs, smartphones, tablets, laptops, monitors, automotive systems, VR/XR, and commercial displays. With a clear strategic direction set by its advanced display technology brand APEX, TCL CSOT invests continuously and strategically in R&D, driven by a mission to amaze, protect and inspire all people through endlessly innovative display technology. As part of TCL's Worldwide Olympic Partnership, TCL CSOT is proud to deliver display solutions that elevate experiences on the global stage.

data.title: I've been married for 58 years. It's 'our' money, not 'his' and 'hers.' Why do so many couples keep their finances separate?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'My wife stopped working outside the home in 1970'

"We have never worried about each other overspending or incurring debt." (Photo subjects are models.)

Dear Quentin,

As a regular reader of The Moneyist, I am puzzled by letters from married couples that talk about his money and her money, her spending and his saving; he shares but she doesn't, or vice versa; and money issues that seem to portray two people living separate financial lives, not a married couple, not ours, but yours and mine. I don't get it.

To put that in perspective, I am 83 and we have been married for 58 years. My wife stopped working outside the home in 1970. In all those years, every money decision has been a joint one; every dollar has been ours; and bank and investment accounts are joint. We have never worried about each other overspending or incurring debt.

Are we just abnormal, or is it a generational thing?

Happily Married

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: My husband is happily retired at 64 and thinks I should keep working. Is he being fair?

The share of couples that did not have any joint bank accounts rose by more than half over the last 30 years.

Dear Happily,

Yes. That's the short answer. Now for the longer one.

Older couples have joint accounts for a variety of reasons. Among them: Women traditionally were more likely to work as homemakers, and the money earned by the breadwinner was for the whole family; couples 30-plus years ago had bigger families that encouraged pooling of resources; and the longer people stay together, the more incentive they have to trust that they will stay together and plan for their future as a team. Second marriages typically have a higher rate of separate accounts.

I would caution against assuming that all letters to this column reflect definite trends in society. While a larger share of younger couples do have separate accounts, as it happens, the nitpicking, if you want to call it that, can lead to moral and ethical dilemmas, differences in spending and saving, suspicion and financial infidelity. One partner might spend money on a new watch or piece of jewelry without telling their partner, leading to questions about fiscal responsibility.

To put some context to your hunch: The share of couples without joint bank accounts rose by more than half, from 15% in 1996 to roughly 23% three decades later, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. Some of the theories given: Couples now tend to marry later when their finances are already established, making them less likely to merge accounts. In 1996, the median age at first marriage was 24.8 years for women and 27.1 years for men. Today, it's about three years older than that.

Related: 'They hate our generation': My son and daughter-in-law want us to sell our house - and move to Oregon to start a commune

Trust in joint accounts

The more faith you have that your marriage will last - it is a legal partnership - the more sense it makes to have joint accounts. That's the takeaway from this analysis by U.S. News and World Report. "With joint accounts, spending can be easily viewed by both spouses, and that level of openness can be reassuring," it says. Though those with separate accounts also may have open and honest relationships, it may be that the most harmonious relationships tend to lean toward joint accounts."

Family finances are, arguably, easier to manage with joint accounts. "Too many bank accounts can muddy the waters and make it difficult to properly track spending and pinpoint areas where a family's budget could be improved," it adds. "Couples may also want to keep joint accounts because they ensure both spouses can access money at any time. If only one person's name is on an account and that spouse becomes injured or ill, their partner may be unable to pull out money needed for medical expenses."

People getting married today come with a lot more baggage.

People getting married today come with a lot more baggage - student debt, individual mortgages because they may have gotten married later in life and disparate credit scores - so separate accounts can protect the wealthier spouse. In the early days of your marriage, your money management was more tangible and a joint effort: You probably used checkbooks and cash together, drove to the supermarket together, and bought clothes in department stores together (or maybe you waited in the car).

Your wife also stopped working full-time outside the home in 1970, which was four years before the Equal Credit Opportunity Act of 1974 that prevented people from being discriminated against by credit-card companies for their race or color, religion, national origin, marital status, age and, last but not least, gender. Opportunities for women and, by inference, dual-income households increased over the following five decades, even if the gender pay gap proves stubbornly hard to close.

Related: 'It feels like he's quietly building a separate life': My husband inherited $500,000, but he refuses to spend it on our home

Lessons from your parents

Fair enough, but the other part of the story - your story - is not reflected in the research or statistics: luck and good fortune. You married the right woman, and she married the right man. You remained committed to your financial goals and true to your personal commitments. As a result, you divided the responsibility of raising and paying for a family, and paid for it as you went along. You are part of the tail end of the Silent Generation, so you know a thing or two about saving and being thrifty.

You were probably raised by either a member of the Silent Generation or the Greatest Generation. They were given their names for good reason. Members of the Greatest Generation were born roughly between 1901 and 1924. They came of age during the Great Depression and fought in World War II. The Silent Generation, born roughly between 1925 and 1945, grew up with the lessons of the previous generation who worked for everything they earned and reaped the rewards of the postwar boom.

A hybrid model of household management allows couples to have both separate and joint accounts and that extra account, if they can afford it, for "mad money" to be used on frivolous expenses. I hope you don't mind me saying that you may have a slight "success bias" - your marriage lasted the test of time and you achieved a financially solid retirement. Many couples in your generation were not so lucky: They fought, they divorced, and they took what they could get from the marriage.

Everyone's normal looks different, including when it comes to shared finances.

Related: 'He calls my plans a fantasy': My husband says we can't afford a $200,000-a-year retirement. Is he being cheap?

data.title: SDLG Group Holds Global Brand Launch Event in Shanghai
data.description:
SDLG Group Holds Global Brand Launch Event in Shanghai

SDLG Group Holds Global Brand Launch Event in Shanghai

PR Newswire

SHANGHAI, Nov. 26, 2026

Group unveils its new global brand strategy under the theme "United for a Century Legacy"

SHANGHAI, Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SDLG Group today unveiled its new global brand strategy, "ONE SDLG," alongside a unified brand architecture and a new visual identity ahead of bauma CHINA 2026. The launch marks a strategic shift from business coordination to a shared vision across the group's operations.

Competition in the global construction equipment industry now extends across the entire value chain. Building on more than 50 years of manufacturing experience, SDLG Group is bringing its businesses together under a unified brand strategy. Looking ahead, the Group has set an RMB 100 billion target for 2030. The group plans to expand its global manufacturing network and accelerate the development of new energy equipment and intelligent machines.

Wang Zhizhong, Honorary Chairman of SDLG Group and Chairman of SDLG, highlighted the group's long-standing commitment to "Forge a Renowned Brand, Build a Century Legacy." Guided by its core brand promise of "Reliability in Action," SDLG Group has grown into one of China's leading construction equipment manufacturers and a globally competitive comprehensive equipment manufacturing group.

Customers from Brazil and China shared their experiences with SDLG's equipment and service support, demonstrating how these principles translate into practice.

Fernando Fagundes, Executive Director of the Board at Brazil's Fagundes Construção e Mineração, highlighted the partnership established at bauma 2025 in Munich. Following field trials, the company placed volume orders for LGMG's CMT106H mining trucks and RTH100 hybrid mining trucks. More than 100 LGMG hybrid mining trucks are now operating at Brazilian mines, with a payload capacity of up to 90 metric tons per truck and overall fuel savings of more than 30%. Fernando Fagundes also praised LGMG's local service capabilities and round-the-clock support.

Li Shengjie, Deputy General Manager of Xinfa Group, reflected on nearly 20 years of cooperation with SDLG. The partnership began with comparative field tests of equipment from several manufacturers during Xinfa's facility expansion. Today, more than 500 SDLG machines support Xinfa's core operations. Mr. Li attributed the long-standing partnership to equipment reliability and full-lifecycle service.

Wang Xin, Rotating Chairman and Executive Chairman of SDLG Group, outlined how the new brand strategy extends reliability beyond product performance to research and development, manufacturing, marketing and service. She identified three priorities: ensuring consistent product quality, delivering customer value throughout the equipment lifecycle and building a collaborative ecosystem centered on green and intelligent technologies and deeper local operations.

With the new logo unveiled, SDLG presents a unified identity as "ONE SDLG," embarking on a new 50-year journey of high-quality growth.

In the future, SDLG Group will continue to drive its growth through product excellence, intelligent innovation, full-lifecycle support and industry-wide collaboration. The group will continue to develop high-end equipment and advance new energy and intelligent technologies, staying true to its core brand promise of "Reliability in Action." Together with its global partners, SDLG Group aims to build a world-class construction equipment brand.

data.title: PRIME BPM Unveils AI Agents 2.0 to Accelerate Business Process Management and Transformation
data.description:
PRIME BPM Unveils AI Agents 2.0 to Accelerate Business Process Management and Transformation

Enhanced AI capabilities deliver 90%+ process map quality, multilingual support, and faster documentation, with conversational mapping and advanced analysis on the horizon.

PRIME BPM, a leading provider of end-to-end AI-powered Business Process Management software, has announced AI Agents 2.0, the next evolution of its four AI agents launched in January 2026. Building on strong adoption across industries, the latest advancements enhance AI-powered process mapping and documentation to help organizations accelerate BPM and operational excellence initiatives.

The enhancements improve AI-generated process quality, reduce manual effort, and make BPM activities more intuitive and accessible.

Key enhancements delivered include:

  • 90%+ process map quality: Improved MapAI capabilities deliver higher-quality BPMN process maps, with support for external lanes and message events.
  • Multilingual and voice-powered mapping: Users can describe processes through voice input and generate maps in 30+ languages, including languages different from the source content.
  • Enhanced Image-to-Map: MapAI captures 100% of identified process content from source images and PDFs, reducing manual corrections.
  • Faster, context-aware SOP generation: AI Procedure Writer combines on-screen context with voice input to generate more relevant procedures.

The added capabilities build on real-world adoption of PRIME BPM's AI agents. A leading bank mapped nearly 4,000 processes in under a month, while a leading aerospace manufacturing organization reported an estimated 70% reduction in mapping time by converting Post-it notes into structured process maps.

Expanding Conversational and Cross-Process Analysis Capabilities

PRIME BPM is developing capabilities that will allow users to build and refine process maps through natural-language conversations and generate supporting procedures alongside process maps.

Planned enhancements to its Digital Process Analyst include richer process analysis using procedures, task attributes, and other process information, alongside library-level analysis to identify improvement opportunities across multiple processes.

"AI is fundamentally changing how organizations approach BPM," said Mark Khabe, Co-Founder of PRIME BPM. "With these advancements, we're making it faster and easier for teams to discover, map, document, and analyze processes using AI, reducing manual effort and accelerating meaningful improvement and transformation outcomes."

PRIME BPM continues to advance its AI capabilities to make business process management faster, more accessible, and scalable across organizations.

About PRIME BPM

PRIME BPM is a cloud-based, AI-powered Business Process Management platform that helps organizations map, analyze, improve, and monitor business processes. Combining BPM, Lean, Six Sigma, and AI technologies, PRIME BPM helps organizations accelerate operational excellence and business transformation initiatives.

data.title: We are living in perilous times if Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang dictates your 401(k) balance
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

Why did a futurist with Huang's prescient vision build a company where all roads lead to him?

The turmoil in markets is a cautionary tale of putting so much power in the hands of one man.

Jensen Huang said he'd do better this time. Not everyone is resting easily.

He helped fuel the global AI revolution from the helm of one of the world's most powerful companies. When he became embroiled in a national-security scandal, the fallout led to a couple of trillion dollars in paper losses, give or take a billion. Before his resignation more than two weeks ago, Huang acknowledged that he had an affair with a woman who has been accused of being a Chinese spy; since then, there were reports of two more affairs with female Nvidia employees.

A Moneyist reader asks if any readers are as vulnerable to Nvidia's fortunes as the global economy appears to be. "Did Nvidia's (NVDA) turmoil put your wealth at risk?" the reader asks. "Whose future wealth depends on one man's personal life? I know some people will be deliberately extra when they respond - of course, my whole portfolio didn't tank. Like most people, I'm diversified. But isn't it interesting how our 401(k)s can be affected by one guy in a black leather jacket?"

A 401(k) with 60% to 80% equity exposure lost roughly 5.5% to 7.5% of its on-paper value.

Even before a cloud of uncertainty enveloped Nvidia, the broader AI market and - eventually - the entire stock market, the average retirement balance had fallen in value in the third quarter of the year. The average 401(k) balance in the quarter fell 2% to $152,500, according to an analysis by Fidelity Investments released Monday. IRA balances dropped by 1% to $142,261, while the average 403(b) balance fell by 2% to $142,100.

Based on the S&P 500's SPX 9.3% decline between Nov. 11 and Nov. 20, a typical 401(k) with 60% to 80% equity exposure lost roughly 5.5% to 7.5% of its on-paper value. On an average $152,500 balance, as reported by Fidelity, that translates to $8,500 to $11,350 - or $600 billion to $800 billion across all 401(k) plans. With markets rallying on Monday on the news of Huang's return, 401(k), IRA and 403(b) accounts recovered a portion of those paper losses, though the durability of that rebound is no sure thing.

The turmoil in markets is a cautionary tale of putting so much power in the hands of one man. Huang returned to his role after President Donald Trump implored Nvidia's board of directors to reinstate their former CEO. The board ultimately complied to restore stability to the share price, despite lingering concerns about Huang's governance. Even so, Huang, who presides over a reported 60 direct reports, had not mentored any clear heir apparent.

Related: I hate that Jensen Huang is back at Nvidia, but I love what it's done for my 401(k). Am I a hypocrite?

All roads lead to Huang

The stock bounced back, at least when his return was initially announced, in part because Trump believes Nvidia and Huang go together like salt and pepper and are key to the continuing AI boom and the health of the U.S. economy. He has reason to feel this way: The Brookings Institution estimates that investment in data-center buildings, power systems, networking infrastructure, microchips and other equipment will hit $10.3 trillion from 2025 to 2032, or roughly 3.63% of gross domestic product per year.

Members of the Moneyist Facebook (META) Group painted a grim picture of this moment. This reader is unsettled by the concentration of market power: "Since the advent of the atom bomb, all futures have been at risk from the whims of one man." And try this on for size: "Anyone who invests in the market is at the whim of the billionaires. Elon Musk tweets and things go berserk." And lastly: "It's always been a risk. Potentially 100 million Americans are invested in Nvidia through mutual funds and retirement accounts."

President Trump believes that Nvidia and Huang go together like salt and pepper.

Huang is instrumental to Nvidia's success and built it into an AI behemoth. In a few short years, he has become a globally recognized tech leader in the iconic style of the late Steve Jobs - even down to the silhouette. Jobs wore his signature black turtleneck and Huang sports a dashing black leather jacket, although he chose a softer, warmer material when he made his triumphant return to Nvidia's HQ in Santa Clara (reportedly a navy cotton Dior shirt).

And yet a futurist with Huang's prescient vision still built a company where all roads lead to him. As tech analyst Daniel Bader noted on CTV News, this is the same man who lied about the affair to his employees, his board of directors, and the general public. "I think that Jensen Huang is the only person who can lead the current version of Nvidia," Bader said, "and I think that coming to terms with that fact was very difficult for both the broader market and internally."

I'm willing to guess that CEOs who neglect to groom successors and perhaps compartmentalize their strategies, supply-chain command and dealmaking do not do so accidentally, but to maintain a tight grip on the corporate helm because their identity is inextricably tied to their role - and the power it brings them. And so here we are. Ultimately, shareholders believed that Nvidia's mission and that of the many tech companies tied to the growth of AI were at risk absent Huang's leadership.

His greatest feat may be making himself irreplaceable - or at least making us all believe that he is.

Related: Is Social Security a Ponzi scheme? No. Don't get carried away with 1930s-era prophecies of doom.

By submitting your story to Dow Jones & Co., the publisher of MarketWatch, you understand and agree that we may use your story, or versions of it, in all media and platforms, including via third parties.

More columns from Quentin Fottrell:

'I've been a stay-at-home mom': I'm 50 and have a chronic illness. My husband lost his job. Should he raid his 401(k)?

I'm terrified of a market crash. Should I put $400,000 of my $1 million retirement savings into an annuity?

We have a $300,000 mortgage with a 2.75% interest rate. I want to pay it off. My husband says I'm crazy. Who's right?

-Quentin Fottrell
